brief.headline: Aluminium's premium for prompt metal more than doubled to a five-week high and the price cleared the top of its four-week range - but the whole base-metals board tightened with it this session, so the bid is for prompt units generally rather than for aluminium in particular.
bullets: WHAT MOVED. The exchange settled aluminium cash at $3,352.00 a tonne on Wednesday, up $27.00 or 0.81%, the highest cash settlement since 11-August and a cumulative $59.50 or 1.81% across three consecutive higher sessions. Three-month rose $19.00 to $3,338.00. Because the front rose more than the back, the premium for metal today over metal in three months - the backwardation - MORE THAN DOUBLED FROM $6.00 TO $14.00, the widest since 04-August and the third consecutive session it has widened.

WHY IT MATTERS. A backwardation means buyers are paying more for metal now than for metal later, which is what a market does when it needs units it cannot easily get. What makes this one unusual is that it widened again while exchange warehouse stock did not move by a single tonne - 244,525 tonnes for the third consecutive session with a published change of exactly zero, and the fourth consecutive reading at the same number. Inventory is at a thirty-six-year low, but the draw that got it there has stopped completely. Level and flow are now telling opposite stories and both are true.

THE PART THAT CHANGED THE READ. Yesterday aluminium was the only metal on the exchange board whose curve tightened, which looked like a metal-specific signal. Today four of the five tightened together: zinc's backwardation widened to $150, copper's to $40 even though its price fell, and lead's contango narrowed; only nickel loosened. That makes aluminium's move corroborated rather than exceptional - a complex-wide bid for prompt metal, which is a weaker and more macro explanation. Scale still matters: aluminium pays 0.42% of its price for prompt units, zinc pays 3.58%, and aluminium has the lowest relative inventory of the two.

WHAT TO WATCH. The European Central Bank decides today with a rise fully priced and the guidance the only live content; the US Federal Reserve follows on 16-September with the US ten-year yield at a three-year high. Brent has topped $100 and European gas has firmed for a third straight session, so the same Gulf disruption that supports the metal price is raising the cost of producing and shipping it. And the October-December Asian quarterly premium is still unsettled, with producers offering $310-325 a tonne against buyers targeting below $300 - the clearest public read available on whether physical Asia is as tight as the London curve now implies.

kpis.note: THURSDAY 10-SEPTEMBER COMPILE, TAKEN BEFORE THE LONDON RING; TODAY'S OWN OFFICIAL PRINTS AT 13:20 LONDON. THE BOARD PUBLISHED THIS MORNING IS THE 09-SEPTEMBER-2026 OFFICIAL AND THE WHOLE PAGE SITS ON THAT ONE UNIFORM SESSION. THE SOURCE STATE IS CLEAN FOR THE SECOND CONSECUTIVE RUN, WHICH HAS NOT HAPPENED SINCE JULY. The English overview and the German overview, each requested with its own cache-busting query string, both carry the 09-September board and agree line for line across all six metals, all six warehouse lines and all three EUR/USD fixings. Every number published here is verified against two independent presentations of the same source. CASH $3,352.00 IS THE 09-SEPTEMBER OFFICIAL, UP $27.00 OR +0.81% ON TUESDAY'S $3,325.00. IT IS THE HIGHEST CASH SETTLEMENT SINCE 11-AUGUST, WHEN THE METAL SETTLED $3,373.00, AND IT CLEARS THE 10-AUGUST HIGH OF $3,327.50 THAT THE PAGE FLAGGED YESTERDAY AS THE LAST STEP IN THE FOUR-WEEK RANGE. THAT STEP HAS NOW BEEN TAKEN. THIS IS THE THIRD CONSECUTIVE HIGHER CASH SETTLEMENT - $3,310.00 on 07-September, $3,325.00 on 08-September and $3,352.00 on 09-September - and a cumulative $59.50 advance from Friday's $3,292.50, a rise of 1.81% across three sessions. THE MOVE IS STATED WITH ITS LIMIT ATTACHED: the metal is now $21.00 below the 11-August settlement and $503.00 below the 02-June high of $3,855.00, so this is the top of a four-week range being cleared rather than a new cycle high being made.

kpis.label: LME 3-month
kpis.note: THREE-MONTH SETTLED $3,338.00 ON 09-SEPTEMBER, UP $19.00 OR +0.57%, ITS OWN HIGHEST SINCE 11-AUGUST WHEN IT CLOSED $3,374.00. THE FORWARD ROSE LESS THAN THE CASH - $19.00 AGAINST $27.00 - AND THAT $8.00 DIFFERENCE IS THE ENTIRE STORY OF THE SESSION, because it is what widened the backwardation. A market that is bidding the front harder than the back is paying for metal it wants now rather than metal it wants later. THE THREE-MONTH IS THE CONTRACT THE FORWARD MODEL AND THE ELLIOTT WAVE COUNT ARE ANCHORED ON, and at $3,338.00 it sits $36.00 below the 11-August impulse high of $3,374.00, which remains the cleanest published upside trigger on the technical panel.

kpis.label: Cash-3M spread
kpis.note: CASH SETTLED $14.00 ABOVE THREE-MONTH - A BACKWARDATION, AND THE CONVENTION IS STATED EXPLICITLY BECAUSE THE SIGN MATTERS: cash above three-month is BACKWARDATION and signals prompt tightness; cash below is CONTANGO. THE SPREAD MORE THAN DOUBLED FROM $6.00 TO $14.00 AND IS THE WIDEST BACKWARDATION SINCE 04-AUGUST, when it printed $34.50. It has now widened on three consecutive sessions from a $0.50 contango on 04-September, through $2.00 and $6.00, to $14.00. THE AUGUST AVERAGE SPREAD WAS A $1.60 CONTANGO, so the current print is more than nine dollars clear of the month it followed. THE SCALE CAVEAT IS KEPT IN PLACE AND IT IS NOT A FORMALITY: $14.00 on a $3,352 metal is forty-two hundredths of one percent. That is a real and now-persistent signal rather than noise, but it is still an order of magnitude smaller than the $150.00 zinc is paying on the same board. SPREAD AND FLAT PRICE MOVED IN THE SAME DIRECTION TODAY - both up - so there is no divergence to flag in aluminium; the divergence on this board is in COPPER, where the flat price FELL while the backwardation WIDENED, which is discussed on the cross-metal row.

kpis.label: LME stocks (t)
kpis.note: EXCHANGE STOCK WAS UNCHANGED AT 244,525 TONNES ON 09-SEPTEMBER - A PUBLISHED CHANGE OF EXACTLY ZERO FOR THE THIRD CONSECUTIVE SESSION AND THE FOURTH CONSECUTIVE PUBLISHED READING AT THE IDENTICAL NUMBER, running back to 04-September. ACROSS THE FIFTEEN SESSIONS FROM 19-AUGUST TO 09-SEPTEMBER STOCK HAS FALLEN 2,400 TONNES, ABOUT 160 TONNES A SESSION, AND ALL OF THAT DRAW HAPPENED BEFORE 04-SEPTEMBER. THE LEVEL AND THE FLOW HAVE NOW FULLY SEPARATED AND THIS IS THE MOST IMPORTANT UNCOMFORTABLE FACT ON THE PAGE: the thirty-six-year low is real and is the strongest single support under the price, but the draw that produced it has stopped completely. A market that is being drained does not print the same tonne four times. WHAT MAKES THIS SESSION DIFFERENT FROM THE LAST THREE IS THAT THE CURVE TIGHTENED ANYWAY, AND MORE SHARPLY: the backwardation more than doubled on stock that did not move by a single tonne, which is direct evidence that prompt demand can firm without the warehouse series registering it at all. THE COUNTER-EVIDENCE IS CARRIED FOR BALANCE: Shanghai inventories were reported down 3% week on week, so the two visible inventory series still disagree with each other.

kpis.label: EUR/USD (LME FX fixing)
kpis.note: THE LME FX FIXING ROSE TO 1.16460 FROM 1.16140, AND THE ECB FIXING ROSE FURTHER STILL TO 1.16520 FROM 1.16140 - THE EURO FIRMED INTO THE EUROPEAN CENTRAL BANK DECISION THAT LANDS TODAY. A firmer euro makes a dollar-priced metal cheaper for a European buyer and marginally cheaper in euro terms for a European smelter's revenue line, which cuts against the region's rising energy cost rather than with it. THE THIRD FIXING ON THE BOARD, THE BFIX REFERENCE RATE, WAS UNCHANGED AT 1.16121 FOR A SECOND SESSION, and that divergence between a moving LME/ECB fix and a static BFIX is normal rather than a source problem - the three fixings are struck at different times of day.

lme.commentary: THE 09-SEPTEMBER SESSION DID THE THING THIS PAGE HAS BEEN WAITING SEVERAL WEEKS TO SEE, AND THEN IMMEDIATELY COMPLICATED IT. Cash settled $3,352.00, up $27.00 or 0.81%, the highest cash official since 11-August; three-month settled $3,338.00, up $19.00, its own highest since 11-August. That is the third consecutive higher settlement and a cumulative $59.50, or 1.81%, from Friday's $3,292.50. Yesterday this page observed that cash sat $2.50 below the 10-August high of $3,327.50 with one small step left to clear the four-week range. THE STEP HAS BEEN TAKEN AND CLEARED BY $24.50. THE STRUCTURE IS WHERE THE INFORMATION IS. The front rose $27.00 while the back rose $19.00, and that $8.00 differential MORE THAN DOUBLED THE BACKWARDATION FROM $6.00 TO $14.00 - the widest since 04-August. Cash above three-month is backwardation and means the market is paying a premium for metal today rather than metal in three months. IT HAS NOW WIDENED ON THREE CONSECUTIVE SESSIONS: a $0.50 contango on 04-September, $2.00 on 07-September, $6.00 on 08-September, $14.00 on 09-September. THREE SESSIONS IS A SHORT TREND RATHER THAN A SINGLE OBSERVATION, and that is the substantive change in the evidence base. The August average spread was a $1.60 CONTANGO, so the current print is more than nine dollars clear of the month that preceded it. AND IT WIDENED AGAIN ON EXCHANGE STOCK THAT DID NOT MOVE. Inventory was unchanged at 244,525 tonnes for the third consecutive session - a published change of exactly ZERO - and the fourth consecutive reading at the identical number. Across the fifteen sessions from 19-August to 09-September the series fell 2,400 tonnes, about 160 a session, and ALL of that draw happened before 04-September. THE LEVEL AND THE FLOW NOW TELL OPPOSITE STORIES AND BOTH ARE TRUE: the thirty-six-year low is the strongest structural support under the price, and the draw that produced it has stopped completely. A market being actively drained does not print the same tonne four times running. What the three-session spread sequence adds is direct evidence that prompt demand can firm without the warehouse series registering it at all - which is either a sign that the visible inventory is no longer the binding constraint, or a sign that the tightness is in positioning rather than in metal. THIS PAGE CANNOT YET DISTINGUISH THOSE TWO AND DOES NOT PRETEND TO. ONE CLAIM MADE YESTERDAY IS WITHDRAWN TODAY. On 08-September aluminium was the ONLY metal on the board whose curve tightened, and that was treated here as a distinguishing signal. On 09-September FOUR OF THE FIVE TIGHTENED - zinc's backwardation from $106.00 to $150.00, copper's from $32.00 to $40.00 even as its flat price FELL $65.00, lead's contango narrowing from $47.00 to $37.00 - while only nickel loosened, its contango widening to $155.00. THE ALUMINIUM MOVE IS THEREFORE CORROBORATED BY THE COMPLEX RATHER THAN DISTINGUISHED FROM IT, which is a weaker and more macro explanation than yesterday's, and it is stated that way deliberately. COPPER IS THE ONE ROW WHERE SPREAD AND FLAT PRICE MOVED IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS and that is flagged explicitly per convention: a market letting go of the back while holding the front, with 1,900 tonnes leaving the warehouse on the same session. THE SCALE CAVEAT IS KEPT AND IT REMAINS THE STRONGEST ARGUMENT FOR RESTRAINT: $14.00 on a $3,352 metal is forty-two hundredths of one percent, against zinc's $150.00 on $4,186 which is 3.58%. Aluminium has the lowest relative inventory on the board and pays the second-smallest prompt premium on it - and zinc is paying its enormous premium while taking metal INTO warehouse. THE MACRO CONTEXT MAKES THE ADVANCE MORE RATHER THAN LESS NOTABLE: the US ten-year printed 4.812% and is carried as a three-year high, and European equity indices fell across the board, yet the metal rose 0.81% into that.

drivers.text: THE TARIFF LEG IS RECOMPUTED EVERY RUN AND IT MOVED TODAY WITHOUT ANY PREMIUM BEING REASSESSED — The US Midwest duty-paid row is carried at its last dated public assessment of $2,094/t. At the verified Section 232 rate of 50% on aluminium articles, the arithmetic tariff leg on today's $3,352.00 exchange cash is $1,676.00, leaving an IMPLIED MARKET LEG of $418.00. Yesterday the same assessment against a $3,325.00 cash gave a tariff leg of $1,662.50 and a market leg of $431.50. THE IMPLIED MARKET LEG THEREFORE NARROWED BY $13.50 TODAY PURELY BECAUSE THE EXCHANGE PRICE ROSE WHILE THE ASSESSMENT STAYED STILL. That is a mechanical artefact of a static periodic assessment against a moving daily benchmark, not a change in US physical tightness, and it is disclosed as such rather than presented as a market signal.

drivers.text: THE PENDING ASIAN QUARTERLY SETTLEMENT IS THE ONLY DRIVER ON THIS PANEL THAT CAN MOVE A LARGE NUMBER IN ONE STEP — Producers including Rio Tinto and South32 offered $310-325/t for October-December against the Q3 record of $395/t, down 18-22%, with Japanese buyers targeting below $300. The gap between the two published positions is roughly $25-45/t and the talks are reported to run through later this month. THE REASON THIS MATTERS BEYOND ASIA is that the Japanese quarterly premium is the regional benchmark for the Pacific basin, so a settlement well below $325 would be the first hard public evidence that the physical tightness narrative has begun to break somewhere, even as the London curve tightens.

prices.note: Carried at its last dated public assessment; NO NEWER DATED PUBLIC MARK PRINTED INTO THE 09-SEPTEMBER COMPILE WINDOW and nothing has been interpolated or estimated. THE ASSESSMENT DATE IS SHOWN ON THE ROW SO THE STALENESS IS VISIBLE RATHER THAN IMPLIED. THE PUBLIC FORWARD VIEW IS UNCHANGED AND REMAINS THE MOST USEFUL PART OF THIS PANEL: SMM expects the SEPTEMBER MONTHLY AVERAGE ALUMINA PRICE TO DECLINE, describing a market entering September in surplus with high operating capacity and continued inventory buildup keeping absolute prices under pressure. THE STRUCTURAL READ IS OTHERWISE UNCHANGED: the refinery side of the chain remains in surplus while the smelter side is disrupted, and Alunorte has ramped back to full capacity from its August 50% cut on a TEMPORARY terminal-access agreement with its gas supplier. WHAT CHANGED THIS RUN IS NOT THE MARK BUT THE FRAGILITY OF THAT ARRANGEMENT, and the evidence sits on the macro panel rather than here: the agreement is a gas arrangement, and crude rose to a three-month high with Brent above $98 on renewed US-Iran escalation while European gas firmed 2.29% for a second consecutive session, a cumulative 4.2%. A TEMPORARY GAS ACCOMMODATION IS MORE FRAGILE IN A TIGHTENING GAS MARKET THAN IN A LOOSENING ONE, so the single largest identifiable upside risk to alumina - and therefore the largest downside risk to smelter margin - is modestly higher this morning even though no alumina number moved. FOR A COST READER THE IMPORTANT NUANCE THIS MONTH IS THAT THE STACK IS MOVING TWO WAYS AT ONCE - SMM expects prebaked anode and aluminium fluoride prices to RISE over the same period, and the energy tape now pushes the same way as the auxiliaries, so a falling alumina headline does not by itself imply a falling total cash cost.  || 10-SEPTEMBER UPDATE: still no newer dated public assessment; the row is HELD at its stated assessment date and nothing has been interpolated. An alumina index correction quoting $338.15/t FOB Australia dated 11-September was found and REJECTED as a prior-year notice, because 11-September is tomorrow.

logistics.note: CARRIED AT ITS LAST PUBLISHED MARK AND THE ASSESSMENT DATE IS SHOWN. CONTAINER FREIGHT IS THE WRONG INDEX FOR PRIMARY METAL AND IS RETAINED FOR THE DOWNSTREAM LEG: extrusions, rolled coil, finished components and value-added products move in boxes rather than in bulk. IT IS THEREFORE THE FREIGHT LINE THAT BEARS ON THE FABRICATED-PRODUCT PREMIUMS ON THIS PAGE - Rotterdam billets, Southeast Asian billet premiums - rather than on the LME price.

logistics.label: Incoterms / demurrage
logistics.note: GENERIC COMMERCIAL NOTE, NOT AN ASSESSMENT, AND UNCHANGED IN SUBSTANCE THIS RUN - BUT WITH A NEW FORWARD-LOOKING POINT WORTH FLAGGING GENERICALLY. Contracts written across the Gulf disruption commonly carry force-majeure, war-risk cost-pass-through and demurrage clauses that were drafted for a CLOSED strait. A partial, temporary, 30-to-60-day corridor arrangement of the kind announced on 26-August sits awkwardly between 'closed' and 'open' and is exactly the situation in which such clauses become contested rather than automatic. Anyone with live tonnage under those terms should expect the interpretation question to arrive before the logistics question resolves. This is a general market observation about contract structure and carries no company-specific or confidential content.

row.label: Brent crude
row.note: BRENT TOPPED $100 AT THIS COMPILE, UP 3.02%, WITH WTI AT $95.47, UP 2.63%. ENERGY IS THE LARGEST SINGLE COST LINE IN A SMELTER AND THE MOST IMPORTANT MACRO ROW ON THIS PAGE FOR A COST READER, AND IT HAS NOW MOVED MATERIALLY ON THREE CONSECUTIVE SESSIONS RATHER THAN DRIFTING - Brent has gone from below $97 through $98 to above $100 in three days. THE RISE IS CONSISTENT WITH RENEWED US-IRAN ESCALATION AND AN UNRESOLVED STRAIT OF HORMUZ SITUATION RATHER THAN WITH DEMAND STRENGTH, which is the uncomfortable combination for this industry: THE SAME DISRUPTION THAT SUPPORTS THE METAL PRICE ALSO RAISES THE COST OF PRODUCING IT AND OF SHIPPING IT. This remains the clearest example on the page of a single variable that is simultaneously bullish for revenue and bearish for margin, and the crossing of the $100 handle matters mainly because it is the level at which energy cost stops being a background assumption in restart economics and becomes the deciding variable.

row.label: European gas TTF
row.note: EUROPEAN GAS FIRMED 3.97% TO EUR 78.85, THE THIRD CONSECUTIVE FIRMING SESSION AND A CUMULATIVE RISE OF ROUGHLY 8.3% ACROSS THE THREE. THIS IS THE ROW THAT DECIDES EUROPEAN RESTART ECONOMICS AND IT IS NOW MOVING THE WRONG WAY FOR THEM AT ACCELERATING PACE. Every European smelter restart in the public pipeline required a power solution before it required a financing decision, and a gas market rising 8.3% in three sessions makes the marginal one harder to sign. IT ALSO BEARS DIRECTLY ON THE ALUMINA SIDE: the world's largest alumina refinery outside China is running at full rate on a TEMPORARY terminal-access agreement with its GAS supplier, and a temporary gas accommodation is more fragile in a tightening gas market than in a loosening one. THE TIMING IS POINTED - the European Central Bank decides today, so the region that must absorb the Russian import ban at year end faces rising energy cost and a tightening policy rate on the same morning.

row.label: US dollar index
row.note: THE DOLLAR INDEX EASED 0.13% TO 98.662, A SECOND CONSECUTIVE SOFTER SESSION. A softer dollar is mechanically supportive for a dollar-priced industrial metal because it makes the same tonne cheaper in every other currency, and it is a small part of why cash could rise 0.81% on a session when the macro backdrop was otherwise hostile. THE EFFECT SHOULD NOT BE OVERSTATED: a 0.13% move in the index is a rounding item against a 0.81% move in the metal, and the dominant dollar story this week is the rate path rather than the spot index. THE HONEST READ IS THAT THE CURRENCY IS A MILD TAILWIND SITTING INSIDE A CLEAR RATE HEADWIND, and the two decisions that will settle which one dominates land today and on 16-September.

row.label: EUR/USD
row.note: THE EURO FIRMED 0.17% TO 1.16442 INTO THE EUROPEAN CENTRAL BANK DECISION THAT LANDS TODAY, and the LME and ECB fixings on the 09-September board corroborate the direction at 1.16460 and 1.16520 against 1.16140 for both on 08-September. A FIRMER EURO IS A MODEST HELP TO A EUROPEAN CONSUMER OF A DOLLAR-PRICED METAL AND A MODEST DRAG ON A EUROPEAN PRODUCER'S EURO REVENUE, and it partially - only partially - offsets the 3.97% rise in European gas on the same session. THE ASYMMETRY IS WORTH STATING: the currency moved 0.17% and the energy input moved 3.97%, so a European cost base got materially worse this session and the exchange-rate offset does not come close to covering it.

row.label: US 10-year Treasury yield
row.note: THE US TEN-YEAR ROSE AGAIN TO 4.812% AND IS NOW CARRIED AS A THREE-YEAR HIGH, WHICH IS AN ESCALATION IN THE DESCRIPTION AS WELL AS IN THE LEVEL - yesterday the same series was carried as a multi-year high. THE BOND MARKET IS PRICING A TIGHTENING PATH RATHER THAN AN EASING ONE AND IT IS DOING SO AHEAD OF TWO DATED DECISIONS: the European Central Bank today and the Federal Reserve on 16-September. FOR A DOLLAR-PRICED INDUSTRIAL METAL THIS IS A DIRECT HEADWIND, and the second-order effect cuts the other way by raising the discount rate on every curtailed-capacity restart decision in the public pipeline - which is bullish for the physical balance even as it is bearish for the price. THAT AMBIGUITY IS REAL AND IS NOT RESOLVED HERE. What is not ambiguous is that the metal rose 0.81% against a three-year-high yield, which says the physical bid is currently strong enough to overcome the macro.

headlines.title: ALUMINIUM SETTLED AT $3,352.00 ON 09-SEPTEMBER, UP $27.00 OR 0.81%, THE HIGHEST CASH OFFICIAL SINCE 11-AUGUST, AND THE BACKWARDATION MORE THAN DOUBLED TO $14.00 - THE WIDEST SINCE 04-AUGUST. Three-month rose $19.00 to $3,338.00, its own highest since 11-August. This is the third consecutive higher cash settlement and a cumulative $59.50, or 1.81%, from Friday's $3,292.50. THE METAL HAS NOW CLEARED THE TOP OF ITS FOUR-WEEK RANGE: yesterday this page noted cash sat $2.50 below the 10-August high of $3,327.50 with one step left to take, and that step has been taken and cleared by $24.50. THE STRUCTURE REMAINS MORE INFORMATIVE THAN THE PRICE: the front rose $27.00 against the back's $19.00, and that $8.00 difference is what widened the spread. THE LIMIT IS ATTACHED TO THE MOVE - $3,352.00 is still $21.00 below the 11-August settlement and $503.00 below the 02-June high of $3,855.00.

FOUR OF THE FIVE METALS ON THE BOARD TIGHTENED THIS SESSION, WHICH WEAKENS RATHER THAN STRENGTHENS THE ALUMINIUM-SPECIFIC READ. Zinc's backwardation widened from $106.00 to $150.00 on cash up $76.00 against three-month up $32.00; copper's widened from $32.00 to $40.00 EVEN THOUGH ITS FLAT PRICE FELL $65.00, because three-month fell $73.00; lead's contango narrowed from $47.00 to $37.00; and aluminium's backwardation more than doubled to $14.00. ONLY NICKEL LOOSENED, its contango widening to $155.00 on unchanged cash. YESTERDAY THIS PAGE ARGUED THAT ALUMINIUM WAS THE ONLY METAL WHOSE CURVE TIGHTENED AND TREATED THAT AS A DISTINGUISHING SIGNAL. TODAY THAT CLAIM NO LONGER HOLDS AND IT IS WITHDRAWN RATHER THAN QUIETLY DROPPED: the complex is bidding for prompt units generally, which is a more macro and less metal-specific explanation. THE SCALE COMPARISON STILL FAVOURS SCEPTICISM - aluminium pays 0.42% of its flat price for prompt metal, zinc pays 3.58%.

EXCHANGE STOCK WAS UNCHANGED AT 244,525 TONNES FOR THE THIRD CONSECUTIVE SESSION - A PUBLISHED CHANGE OF EXACTLY ZERO - AND THE FOURTH CONSECUTIVE READING AT THE IDENTICAL NUMBER. Across the fifteen sessions from 19-August to 09-September the series has fallen 2,400 tonnes, about 160 a session, and ALL of that draw happened before 04-September. THE THIRTY-SIX-YEAR LOW IS REAL AND IS THE STRONGEST STRUCTURAL SUPPORT UNDER THE PRICE; THE DRAW THAT PRODUCED IT HAS STOPPED COMPLETELY. A market being actively drained does not print the same tonne four times running. This is filed as bearish because it removes the flow argument from the bull case, and the level argument is a floor rather than a trigger. Shanghai inventories were separately reported down 3% week on week, so the two visible series still disagree.

BRENT CROSSED $100 A BARREL AT THIS COMPILE, UP 3.02%, WITH WTI UP 2.63% TO $95.47, ON A THIRD CONSECUTIVE SESSION OF GAINS ATTRIBUTED TO RENEWED US-IRAN ESCALATION AND AN UNRESOLVED STRAIT OF HORMUZ SITUATION. Public commentary at this compile put GCC aluminium output down 44% year on year in July. THE MIDDLE EAST DISRUPTION REMAINS THE ONE PILLAR OF THE BULL CASE THAT HAS NOT WEAKENED, and it is corroborated by public company disclosure rather than inferred: Qatalum runs at roughly 60% of its 648,000-tonne nameplate on reduced gas with a force majeure on aluminium sales outstanding, and Aluminium Bahrain has had reduction lines 1, 2 and 3 idled since March 2026, about 19% of 1,623,000 tonnes. NEITHER HAS A PUBLISHED RESOLUTION DATE. THE SECOND-ORDER EFFECT IS NOT SUPPRESSED: the same escalation raises the energy and freight cost of producing and moving metal everywhere else.

THE US TEN-YEAR YIELD ROSE AGAIN TO 4.812% AND IS NOW CARRIED AS A THREE-YEAR HIGH, AN ESCALATION IN DESCRIPTION AS WELL AS IN LEVEL. THE EUROPEAN CENTRAL BANK DECIDES TODAY with a 25 basis point rise fully priced after euro-area August CPI rebounded to 3.3% year on year, and the US Federal Reserve follows on 16-September after August payrolls printed +162,000 against a consensus near 53,000, with traders pricing the possibility of a HIKE. FOR A DOLLAR-PRICED INDUSTRIAL METAL A RISING GLOBAL RATE PATH IS A DIRECT HEADWIND. THE COUNTER-OBSERVATION IS THE MOST INTERESTING THING ON THIS ROW AND IT IS BULLISH: the metal rose 0.81% ANYWAY, against a three-year-high yield and a stock market selling off across every major European index. That says the physical bid is currently strong enough to overcome the macro, which is not something this page has been able to write for several weeks.

CANADA'S COUNTER-TARIFFS COMPLETED THEIR SECOND FULL DAY IN FORCE AND NEITHER SIDE ANNOUNCED FURTHER ESCALATION. Effective 08-September they raised Canadian counter-tariffs on US steel and aluminium from 25% to 50% to match the US rate, inside a package covering $27.6 billion of US imports and more than 300 metals products and derivatives. THE US SECTION 232 RATE WAS RE-VERIFIED THIS RUN AND IS UNCHANGED AT 50% ON ARTICLES AND 25% ON DERIVATIVES. THE MECHANICAL CONSEQUENCE IS DECOUPLING RATHER THAN SIMPLE INFLATION: regional delivered premiums on both sides of the border are supported because arbitrage between them is more expensive, while the volume that actually crosses is suppressed. BECAUSE NO FURTHER ESCALATION CAME, THE ASSOCIATED RISK IS LOWERED FROM RISING TO FLAT ON THE REGISTER - the measure is now known and quantified, and the incremental risk is escalation from here rather than this event.

THE OCTOBER-DECEMBER ASIAN QUARTERLY PREMIUM IS STILL UNSETTLED AND THE PENDING RANGE IS HELD AT $290-325 FOR AN EIGHTH CONSECUTIVE RUN. Producers including Rio Tinto and South32 opened at $310-$325 per tonne against the Q3 record of $395, down 18-22%, with Japanese buyers targeting below $300, on a rationale citing progress on Middle East production and softer European premiums. A FURTHER DATED SEARCH THIS MORNING RETURNED NOTHING NEWER THAN THE 02-SEPTEMBER REPORT, so the range is not narrowed - this page does not tighten a published range on judgement alone. BOTH INPUTS TO THE STATED RATIONALE MOVED AGAINST THE PRODUCERS AGAIN THIS SESSION: the Gulf escalated with Brent through $100, and the exchange curve tightened for a third consecutive session. If the premium settles inside the offered range regardless, that is the strongest available evidence that physical Asia is looser than the London curve implies.

CHINESE EXPORTS REMAIN THE MOST UNDER-WEIGHTED BEARISH FACT ON THIS PAGE AND NO NEWER PUBLIC DATA PRINTED THIS RUN. The latest public figure is a 18.7% year-on-year rise in July, attributed in public commentary to muted domestic demand allowing producers to ship out despite the 45-million-tonne output cap. THE STALENESS IS STATED PLAINLY RATHER THAN GLOSSED: this figure has now been carried unchanged for several runs. THE MECHANISM MATTERS MORE THAN THE NUMBER - the relieving metal arrives as semi-finished and alloy product that never passes through an LME warehouse, which is one coherent explanation for how a thirty-six-year exchange inventory low can coexist with a warehouse series that has not moved a tonne in four readings. WHAT IT DOES NOT EXPLAIN is why the front of the curve has now tightened on three consecutive sessions.

NO NEWER DATED PUBLIC ALUMINA ASSESSMENT PRINTED INTO THIS COMPILE WINDOW AND NOTHING HAS BEEN INTERPOLATED. The FOB East Australia row is carried at its last dated public trade of $356/t on 05-August with the assessment date shown so the staleness is visible. ONE APPARENTLY NEWER FIGURE WAS FOUND AND DELIBERATELY REJECTED: a search returned an alumina index correction notice quoting $338.15/t FOB Australia dated 11-September, which is TOMORROW and therefore cannot be a 2026 mark - it is a prior-year notice and it has NOT been used. THE PUBLIC FORWARD VIEW IS UNCHANGED AND REMAINS THE USEFUL PART OF THIS PANEL: SMM expects the September monthly average alumina price to DECLINE on surplus, high operating capacity and continued inventory buildup, WHILE prebaked anode and aluminium fluoride both RISE. The cost stack is moving in at least two directions at once and total cash cost is not readable from the alumina headline alone.

THE ENERGY SIDE OF THE COST STACK DETERIORATED FOR A THIRD CONSECUTIVE SESSION AND IS NOW THE DOMINANT INPUT STORY. Brent crossed $100, up 3.02%, and European gas TTF rose 3.97% to EUR 78.85, a cumulative advance of roughly 8.3% across three sessions. ELECTRICITY IS TYPICALLY THE LARGEST SINGLE LINE IN A SMELTER'S CASH COST AND CARBON IS THE SECOND, so a move of this size in three days is material to margin regardless of where the metal price goes. IT ALSO RAISES THE OPERATING COST OF EVERY RESTART IN THE PUBLIC PIPELINE AT THE SAME MOMENT THE US TEN-YEAR PRINTS A THREE-YEAR HIGH AND RAISES THE HURDLE RATE ON FINANCING THEM. THE COMFORTABLE READING THAT A FALLING ALUMINA PRICE MEANS A FALLING CASH COST IS LESS TENABLE THIS MONTH THAN LAST, because the auxiliaries and the energy line are now pushing the same way.

THE WESTERN RESTART PIPELINE IS UNCHANGED IN SUBSTANCE AND ONE ENTRY IS WORTH CARRYING EXPLICITLY THIS RUN: MAGNITUDE 7 METALS PLANS TO RESTART ITS MISSOURI PRIMARY SMELTER, WITH THE FIRST POTLINE GUIDED TO COME ONLINE BEFORE THE END OF 2026 AND ADDING ROUGHLY 75,000 TONNES OF ANNUAL CAPACITY, on an investment case that public reporting attributes directly to the 50% US aluminium tariff. THE VOLUME IS SMALL AGAINST A GLOBAL BALANCE MEASURED IN TENS OF MILLIONS OF TONNES; THE MECHANISM IS NOT SMALL. A tariff has made a domestic restart economic that was not economic before, which is the intended effect of the measure and a genuine medium-term bearish input to the US regional premium. ALONGSIDE IT: Slovalco's first 75,000 tonnes of 175,000 guided to Q4-2026, which begins in three weeks; San Ciprian close to full on energy hedged through 2027; Mt Holly at full capacity for the first time since 2015; and EGA with 315 of Al Taweelah's 1,262 cells back online.

THE PRICE SOURCE WAS FULLY CLEAN FOR A SECOND CONSECUTIVE MORNING, WHICH HAS NOT HAPPENED SINCE JULY. The English overview and the German overview, each requested with its own cache-busting query string, both carry the 09-September board and agree line for line across all six metals, all six warehouse lines and all three EUR/USD fixings. ALL FIVE PER-METAL DAILY TABLES - ALUMINIUM, COPPER, NICKEL, ZINC AND LEAD - ALSO CARRY 09-SEPTEMBER AND REPRODUCE THE OVERVIEW EXACTLY, so no figure on this page required the arithmetic reconciliation that the late-August and early-September runs each had to disclose. The stock identity balances five out of five to the tonne against the prior session plus published changes. THE EXPOSURE IS NOT CLOSED BY A CLEAN MORNING: the page still depends on a single primary price source, and the caching and publication-lag failures observed on 31-July, 04-August and across late August were characteristics of that source rather than one-off events.

earnings.note: Revenue RMB 11.53bn, up 32.4% year on year. Net profit attributable to owners RMB 2.30bn, up 166.1%. EPS RMB 1.11 against RMB 0.58 in the corresponding period of last year, up 91.4%. THE CLEANEST PUBLIC READ THIS WEEK ON HOW FAR SMELTER MARGIN HAS EXPANDED AT 2026 PRICES, AND IT COMES FROM AN INTEGRATED, SELF-SUPPLIED PRODUCER. The company operates 788,100 t/y of electrolytic aluminium capacity in Huolinguole, Inner Mongolia with a captive power plant, plus an alumina refining and aluminium hydroxide base in Binzhou, Shandong; it states that self-sufficiency in alumina and electricity fully meets its production requirements. Profit attributable rose 166% on revenue up 32%, which is operating leverage of roughly five times and is only possible when the price rises against a cost base that does not. Management attributes the gain to higher electrolytic aluminium selling prices, lower production cost from a rising green-energy share, and an optimised financing structure. TWO FORWARD DISCLOSURES MATTER BEYOND the quarter: 1,040 MW of wind and 110 MW of solar were commissioned by end-June with the programme roughly 66% complete and the green share expected to exceed 50%, which lowers the cost base further; and the 500,000 t/y integrated electrolytic aluminium project in Saudi Arabia, invested with partners in 2025, had completed all compliance approvals with on-site construction in full swing. That project is a dated, sourced addition to the non-Chinese capacity pipeline. THE UNCOMFORTABLE IMPLICATION FOR PRICE BULLS: margins this wide at the low end of the cost curve are exactly the condition that funds new capacity, and this disclosure shows the funding and the capacity in the same document.

Adjusted EBITDA Dh4.51bn, up 11% from Dh4.07bn, with the adjusted EBITDA margin widening to 33.3% from 27.0%. Profit rose on three named drivers - higher realised aluminium prices, stronger regional premiums and LOWER ALUMINA PRICES - while a third of the sales volume was simply unavailable. A 630 basis-point margin expansion on a 10% revenue decline is only possible when the cost side has fallen faster than the top line, and the alumina leg is the reason. IT ALSO EXPLAINS TODAY'S PRICE ACTION IN ONE LINE: the same release that showed the margin also showed the recovery date, and the market traded the recovery date. earnings.note: RECORD QUARTER ACROSS EVERY SEGMENT. Consolidated revenue RS 84,825cr, up 32% year-on-year; consolidated EBITDA RS 14,989cr, up 73%; net profit RS 7,013cr, up 75%. The EBITDA margin printed 16.42% against 12.31% in Q1 FY26 and 12.82% in Q4 FY26 - a 411 basis-point expansion year-on-year and 360 basis points sequentially. INDIA ALUMINIUM UPSTREAM delivered its highest-ever quarterly EBITDA at RS 7,390cr, up 81%, comfortably exceeding the prior record of RS 5,448cr set in Q4 FY26. The COPPER segment also set a record at RS 918cr, up 36%. NOVELIS, the downstream subsidiary, reported adjusted EBITDA of $516m, up 24% from $416m a year earlier and equivalent to RS 4,875cr (+37%), with net income of $164m (+71%) and adjusted EBITDA of roughly $563 per tonne, helped by the restart of the Oswego hot mill in early June 2026 and continued Bay Minette commissioning. THIS IS THE CLEANEST PUBLIC EVIDENCE AVAILABLE OF HOW AN INTEGRATED PRODUCER CONVERTS THE 2026 PRICE STRUCTURE INTO MARGIN, AND THE CONVERSION RATE IS VERY HIGH. Revenue rose 32% while EBITDA rose 73% and upstream aluminium EBITDA rose 81% - operating leverage of well over two times on the upstream leg. The mechanism is integration: captive bauxite, captive alumina and captive coal-fired power insulate the cost stack from exactly the two legs that are currently rising for non-integrated smelters, namely seaborne bauxite (SMM index $71.57/mt, +$0.70 w/w) and seaborne alumina ($356/mt FOB East Australia on the 05-Aug trade). THE CONTRAST WITH CENTURY IS THE POINT. Century Aluminum, which buys its alumina, has now cited unfavourable raw-material price realisation as its principal EBITDA headwind for two consecutive quarters; Hindalco, which makes its own, posted a record. Management had guided to roughly 5% sequential aluminium cost inflation into this quarter and still delivered a record, which says the LME move more than absorbed it. FOR THE MARKET VIEW: this is bullish for the margin narrative and neutral-to-bearish for the supply narrative, because producers earning at this level have every incentive to run flat out and to accelerate the restart pipeline.

Constellium reported Q2-2026 Adjusted EBITDA of $439 MILLION, a record, taking H1-2026 to $798m, and RAISED FULL-YEAR 2026 GUIDANCE to $980m-$1.020bn of Adjusted EBITDA EXCLUDING METAL PRICE LAG with free cash flow in excess of $300m. Leverage was 1.8x at the quarter end. Management states that the 2028 targets of $900m ex-lag EBITDA and $300m of free cash flow will now be met two years early. THE METAL PRICE LAG IS THE NUMBER THAT MATTERS FOR READING THIS PAGE and it is disclosed by the company: the $439m headline INCLUDES a $129m non-cash benefit from metal price lag, so the ex-lag figure is $310m. The four-quarter ex-lag path is $196m, $213m, $262m, $310m against headline figures of $235m, $280m, $359m and $439m - the gap between the two series has widened every quarter. THE READ-THROUGH IS THE MOST IMPORTANT ONE ON THIS PANEL FOR ANYONE TRYING TO SIZE HOW MUCH OF THE 2026 EARNINGS CYCLE IS REAL. Constellium is a converter, not a smelter: it buys primary and scrap and sells rolled and extruded product, so a rising LME shows up in its results as a NON-CASH metal price lag benefit before it shows up anywhere in the operating business. That lag contributed $126m across the whole of FY2025 and $226m in the FIRST HALF of 2026 alone - it has nearly doubled in half the time. UNDERLYING PERFORMANCE IS GENUINELY GOOD, with ex-lag Adjusted EBITDA up 58% from $196m in Q3-2025 to $310m in Q2-2026 and the company pulling its 2028 targets forward by two years - but a reader who takes the $439m headline as operating performance overstates it by 29%. THE GENERAL POINT EXTENDS ACROSS THIS WHOLE PANEL: a large share of the 2026 aluminium earnings recovery is price-lag and inventory revaluation rather than volume or spread, which is exactly the kind of earnings that reverses when the LME stops rising - and the completed August board, on which aluminium's monthly mean rose 2.97% against copper's 6.12% and zinc's 7.76%, is the first evidence that it may be about to.

Kaiser reported record Q2-2026 adjusted EBITDA of $166.3m against $67.7m a year earlier, a 146% increase, on net sales of $1.2566bn and conversion revenue of $437.0m. GAAP net income was $96.8m or $5.72 per diluted share against $23.2m and $1.41. Adjusted EBITDA margin on conversion revenue doubled to 38.1% from 18.1%. H1-2026 adjusted EBITDA was $294.8m against $141.1m. Net debt leverage improved to 2.1x from 3.4x at 31-December-2025 and the full-year adjusted EBITDA outlook was raised to +45-55% year on year from +20-30%. Shipments rose 6% to 305.7 million lbs, led by packaging at 155.8 million lbs and aerospace/high-strength at 60.8 million. THE READ-THROUGH IS A WARNING ABOUT HOW MUCH OF THE 2026 DOWNSTREAM EARNINGS CYCLE IS A PRICE ARTEFACT RATHER THAN A DEMAND ONE, AND KAISER DISCLOSES IT MORE HONESTLY THAN MOST. Adjusted EBITDA includes management-estimated FAVOURABLE METAL PRICE LAG of approximately $27.0m in Q2-2026 and $36.0m in Q1-2026 - $64.0m across the half against $36.0m in H1-2025. That is roughly 22% of H1-2026 adjusted EBITDA arising from the timing difference between the Midwest Transaction Price embedded in cost of sales and the market price over the period, not from conversion economics. MANAGEMENT SAID SO EXPLICITLY: the raised full-year outlook 'assumes a NEUTRAL metal price lag through the end of the year, and does not assume a continuation of the metal lag or consumption cost tailwinds recorded in the first half', and the CEO said the company expects aluminium price dynamics to normalise over the balance of the year. THE COMMERCIAL LESSON FOR READING THIS WHOLE PANEL: a rising aluminium price inflates downstream converter earnings twice - once through genuine mix and volume, once through inventory timing - and the second half reverses if the price stops rising. Kaiser's underlying story is nevertheless real: conversion revenue per pound rose to $1.43 from $1.30, packaging conversion revenue per pound rose to $1.12 from $0.92, and aerospace shipments grew as destocking eased. Both things are true at once and the filing quantifies the split, which is why this row is worth its place.

trade.note: TRADE CORRIDORS ARE REVIEWED MONTHLY OR ON MATERIAL CHANGE RATHER THAN REFRESHED DAILY. THEY ARE RE-RATED THIS RUN AND THE TRIGGER IS SPECIFIC AND DATED: CANADA'S COUNTER-TARIFFS TAKE EFFECT TODAY, 08-SEPTEMBER-2026, AND EXPLICITLY INCLUDE ALUMINIUM. Canada is applying 15%, 25% and 50% tariffs on products drawn from those targeted by the US Section 338 and Section 232 measures, with each product's rate matched to the corresponding US rate; IN STEEL AND ALUMINIUM THE EXISTING 25% COUNTER-TARIFF RISES TO 50%. The package covers $27.6 billion of US imports and more than 300 metals products and derivatives including flat-rolled steel and aluminium bars, and is described by the Canadian government as matching the US Section 338 tariffs dollar for dollar after the US imposed 50% on $27.6 billion of Canadian goods effective 22-August. WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN A NORMAL TARIFF HEADLINE: the Canada-United States corridor is by volume the most important primary-aluminium trade route in the world, and it is now taxed in BOTH directions rather than one. THE CONSEQUENCE FOR A PHYSICAL READER IS DECOUPLING RATHER THAN SIMPLE INFLATION - regional delivered premiums on both sides of the border are mechanically supported because arbitrage between them is more expensive, while the volume that actually crosses is suppressed, so the delivered price and the exchange benchmark drift further apart. THE SECOND ACTIVE DRIVER IS UNCHANGED AND STILL UNRESOLVED: the latest escalation in US-Iran hostilities has raised uncertainty over any return of Persian Gulf supply, and Middle East LNG scarcity on tanker disruption continues to constrain regional refining and smelting.

flows.note: THE RED SEA IS DIVERGING FROM HORMUZ. On 05-Aug Houthi forces claimed they had targeted a Saudi oil tanker in the Gulf of Aden and threatened further vessels in the Red Sea, with a ship reported hit the same day. Saudi Arabia has been diverting crude to the Suez routing; the Suez leg for Gulf and Red Sea origin cargoes is therefore still not a clean alternative to Hormuz.

catalysts.text: EUROPEAN CENTRAL BANK DECISION - TODAY, DURING THIS SESSION, WITH A 25 BASIS POINT RISE FULLY PRICED. Euro-area August CPI rebounded to 3.3% year on year, the highest since September 2023. BECAUSE THE RISE IS FULLY PRICED THE MARKET-MOVING CONTENT IS THE GUIDANCE, and the risk is two-sided: dovish framing would be read as the end of the cycle, any signal of a follow-up extends the euro-area tightening path into 2027. The euro firmed into it, to 1.16442 spot with the ECB fixing at 1.16520 against 1.16140 the session before. THE EUROPEAN LEG MATTERS DISPROPORTIONATELY HERE because European restart economics are already marginal on energy cost - TTF has firmed roughly 8.3% across three sessions - and because the duty-unpaid premium must absorb the Russian import ban at year end.

US FEDERAL RESERVE DECISION - SIX SESSIONS AWAY AND THE MOST CONSEQUENTIAL SINGLE DATE IN THE NEAR TERM. August payrolls printed +162,000 against a consensus near 53,000, with June and July revised up a combined 55,000, unemployment steady at 4.1% and participation up to 61.6%, and traders moved to price the possibility of a HIKE. THE OPEN QUESTION HAS FLIPPED FROM WHETHER THE FED CUTS TO WHETHER IT RAISES, and the bond market keeps corroborating - the US ten-year at 4.812% is now carried as a THREE-YEAR high, with broad European equity weakness on the same session. Direct headwind for a dollar-priced metal; simultaneously a brake on the restart pipeline through the discount rate, so the net effect on the physical balance is ambiguous even where the effect on price is not. THE COUNTER-OBSERVATION IS ON THE RECORD: the metal rose 0.81% against that backdrop this session.

WHETHER THE BACKWARDATION HOLDS AND WHETHER THE INVENTORY DRAW RESUMES - STILL TWO SEPARATE QUESTIONS, AND THE FIRST HAS NOW PARTLY ANSWERED ITSELF. The spread has widened on THREE consecutive sessions, from a $0.50 contango through $2.00 and $6.00 to $14.00, the widest since 04-August, while stock stayed pinned at 244,525 tonnes for a fourth consecutive reading. THE CONFIRMING COMBINATION IS A RESUMED DRAW ALONGSIDE A BACKWARDATION THAT HOLDS OR WIDENS; that would convert a three-session trend into a tightness regime. THE FALSIFYING COMBINATION IS EQUALLY CLEAR: the spread slipping back inside $2.00 while stock stays flat would mark the whole sequence as positioning rather than physical demand. WATCH ALSO WHETHER ALUMINIUM RE-EARNS THE DISTINCTION IT LOST TODAY - it was the only metal tightening on 08-September, but four of five tightened on 09-September, so the next few sessions decide whether this is an aluminium story or a base-metals story.

RESOLUTION OF THE OCTOBER-DECEMBER ASIAN QUARTERLY PREMIUM, NOW PLAUSIBLY DAYS AWAY. Producers including Rio Tinto and South32 opened at $310-$325 per tonne against the Q3 record of $395, down 18-22%, with Japanese buyers targeting below $300. Talks began the week of 24-August and run through later this month. THE PENDING RANGE HERE IS HELD AT $290-325 AND HAS NOT BEEN NARROWED, for an EIGHTH consecutive run, because no dated public report newer than 02-September printed. BOTH INPUTS TO THE PRODUCERS' STATED RATIONALE MOVED AGAINST THEM AGAIN THIS SESSION: that rationale cited Middle East progress and softer European premiums, but the Gulf escalated with Brent through $100 and the exchange curve tightened for a third consecutive session. IF THE PREMIUM SETTLES INSIDE THE OFFERED RANGE ANYWAY, that is the strongest available evidence that physical Asia is looser than the London curve implies - which is the single most informative dated event on this page.

THE MONTHLY CARBON SETTLEMENT CYCLE, NOW ABOUT A WEEK AWAY. Prebaked anode and coal tar pitch settle monthly on this cadence; the September anode settlement is already public at 5,730 RMB/t spot and 5,745 RMB/t acceptance, above August's 5,630, and coal tar pitch has not printed a newer mark since 13-August. SMM EXPECTS SEPTEMBER ANODE AND ALUMINIUM FLUORIDE BOTH TO RISE WHILE THE MONTHLY AVERAGE ALUMINA PRICE DECLINES, so the cost stack is moving two ways at once. THE ENERGY TAPE NOW PUSHES WITH THE AUXILIARIES RATHER THAN AGAINST THEM - Brent through $100 and European gas up roughly 8.3% across three sessions - which makes the comfortable reading that falling alumina means falling cash cost materially less tenable this month than last. A regional East China spot quotation of RMB 5,230/t was visible this morning and was NOT appended to the anode series, because mixing a regional spot basis into a national settlement series would corrupt the trend rather than extend it.

THE FIRST MEASURABLE TEST OF CANADA'S COUNTER-TARIFFS, WHICH TOOK EFFECT 08-SEPTEMBER AND RAISED CANADIAN COUNTER-TARIFFS ON US STEEL AND ALUMINIUM FROM 25% TO 50%. TWO FULL DAYS HAVE NOW PASSED IN FORCE WITH NO FURTHER ESCALATION FROM EITHER SIDE AND NO NEW DATED ASSESSMENT. The mechanical expectation is support for regional delivered premiums on both sides of the border alongside suppressed cross-border volume. BECAUSE PREMIUM ASSESSMENTS ARE PERIODIC RATHER THAN DAILY, THE EFFECT WILL APPEAR WITH A LAG, and nothing has been written into the premium rows on the strength of the measure alone. The US Midwest duty-paid row is carried at $2,094/t, of which $1,676.00 is the arithmetic tariff leg at a verified 50% rate on today's $3,352 exchange price, leaving an implied market leg of $418.00 - down $13.50 from yesterday purely because the benchmark rose while the assessment stood still.

THE EU IMPORT BAN ON RUSSIAN PRIMARY ALUMINIUM TAKES EFFECT - now under sixteen weeks away. The European duty-unpaid premium is the price that must absorb it, and at a last assessment of $485/t - below its own trailing average of $519.10, with the published rationale for lower Q4 Japanese offers explicitly citing SOFTER European premiums - it is not currently behaving as though the event is coming. Either replacement units are already sourced, or the event is not yet priced; the assessment cadence is too slow to tell which. THE PRESSURE ON THE REPLACEMENT-SUPPLY SIDE INCREASED AGAIN THIS RUN, with European gas up roughly 8.3% across three sessions and the ECB tightening today, both of which narrow the room for European restarts to supply those units. Slovalco's Q4-2026 start is three weeks away and is the nearest European addition standing in that squeeze.

risks.text: RE-ASSESSED 10-SEPTEMBER. LOWERED FROM UP TO FLAT, AND THIS IS A DELIBERATE RE-RATING ON THE ABSENCE OF NEW EVIDENCE RATHER THAN ON ITS PRESENCE. THE RISK AS WRITTEN IS THAT TARIFF POLICY, NOT SUPPLY AND DEMAND, BECOMES THE DOMINANT DETERMINANT OF REGIONAL DELIVERED PRICE. Canada's counter-tariffs took effect 08-September and explicitly include aluminium, raising Canadian counter-tariffs on US steel and aluminium from 25% to 50% to match the US rate, inside a package covering $27.6 billion of US imports and more than 300 metals products and derivatives. THE MEASURE HAS NOW COMPLETED TWO FULL DAYS IN FORCE AND NEITHER GOVERNMENT ANNOUNCED FURTHER ESCALATION. The US Section 232 rate was re-verified this morning and is unchanged at 50% on articles and 25% on derivatives. THE REASON FOR LOWERING TO FLAT IS THAT THE EVENT HAS HAPPENED AND IS NOW KNOWN AND QUANTIFIED: the level of the risk remains HIGH and the consequence - regional delivered premiums supported on both sides of a corridor whose volume is suppressed, decoupling delivered price from the exchange benchmark - is fully live. WHAT HAS STOPPED IS THE RATE OF INCREASE. From here the incremental risk is further escalation by either party, which is a separate and currently unsignalled event. THE HONEST LIMITATION IS THAT THE EFFECT IS NOT YET MEASURABLE: premium assessments are periodic, no new dated US Midwest assessment has printed since the measure took effect, and nothing has been written into the premium rows on the strength of the policy alone.

RE-ASSESSED 10-SEPTEMBER. HELD AT FLAT, AND THE TWO SIDES OF IT MOVED IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS AGAIN. THE RISK AS WRITTEN IS THAT CURTAILED AND DISRUPTED CAPACITY RETURNS FASTER THAN THE MARKET EXPECTS. THE PIPELINE GREW SLIGHTLY THIS RUN: alongside Slovalco's first 75,000 tonnes of 175,000 guided to Q4-2026, Alcoa's San Ciprian close to full on energy hedged through 2027, Portland's 15,000 tonnes completed in Q2-2026, Century's Mt Holly at full capacity for the first time since 2015 and EGA with 315 of Al Taweelah's 1,262 cells back online, public reporting carries MAGNITUDE 7 METALS RESTARTING ITS MISSOURI SMELTER WITH THE FIRST POTLINE GUIDED BEFORE END-2026, ADDING ROUGHLY 75,000 TONNES, on an investment case attributed directly to the 50% US tariff. AGAINST THAT, THE GATING CONDITION WORSENED FOR A THIRD CONSECUTIVE SESSION AND ON BOTH HALVES AT ONCE. Every entry in the pipeline needs a power solution and a financing decision. European gas rose 3.97% to EUR 78.85, a third consecutive rise and roughly 8.3% cumulatively, and the US ten-year printed 4.812% and is now carried as a THREE-YEAR high. THE OPERATING COST AND THE HURDLE RATE OF THE NEXT RESTART DECISION BOTH ROSE AGAIN ON THE SAME SESSION, so a longer announced pipeline is being offset by a harder economic test, and the net risk of faster-than-expected return is unchanged.

RE-ASSESSED 10-SEPTEMBER. HELD AT UP. MACRO TIGHTENING REMAINS THE CLEAREST NEAR-TERM PRICE HEADWIND AND THE FIRST OF THE TWO DATED DECISIONS IS TODAY RATHER THAN TOMORROW. The European Central Bank decides this session with a 25 basis point rise fully priced after euro-area August CPI rebounded to 3.3% year on year, the highest since September 2023; because the rise is priced, the market-moving content is the guidance and the risk is two-sided. The US Federal Reserve follows on 16-September after August payrolls printed +162,000 against a consensus near 53,000, with prior months revised up a combined 55,000 and participation at 61.6%; traders moved to price the possibility of a HIKE. THE BOND MARKET CONTINUED TO CORROBORATE THIS SESSION AND THE DESCRIPTION ESCALATED WITH THE LEVEL: the US ten-year at 4.812% is now carried as a THREE-YEAR HIGH rather than a multi-year high, alongside broad European equity weakness with the DAX down 1.57%, the CAC down 2.00% and the IBEX down 2.35% on the same session. THE ONE PIECE OF GENUINE COUNTER-EVIDENCE IS REPORTED AND IT IS SIGNIFICANT: aluminium rose 0.81% ANYWAY. A dollar-priced industrial metal advancing against a three-year-high yield and a broad risk-off tape says the physical bid is currently strong enough to overcome the macro - which lowers the near-term potency of this risk without lowering its direction.

RE-ASSESSED 10-SEPTEMBER. HELD AT UP AND IT ESCALATED AGAIN, VISIBLY, IN THE ENERGY TAPE FOR A THIRD CONSECUTIVE SESSION. THE MIDDLE EAST DISRUPTION REMAINS THE ONE PILLAR OF THE BULL CASE THAT HAS NOT WEAKENED AT ANY POINT. BRENT CROSSED $100 A BARREL, UP 3.02%, WITH WTI UP 2.63% TO $95.47, on gains attributed to renewed US-Iran escalation and an unresolved Strait of Hormuz situation; public commentary at this compile put GCC aluminium output down 44% year on year in July. THE UNDERLYING CAPACITY LOSS IS OBSERVABLE IN PUBLIC COMPANY DISCLOSURE RATHER THAN INFERRED: Qatalum is at roughly 60% of its 648,000-tonne nameplate on reduced gas with a force majeure on aluminium sales outstanding, and Aluminium Bahrain has had reduction lines 1, 2 and 3 idled since March 2026, about 19% of 1,623,000 tonnes, attributed to Strait transit disruption. NEITHER HAS A PUBLISHED RESOLUTION DATE, which is precisely what distinguishes them from the scheduled restart pipeline. THE CROSSING OF THE $100 HANDLE IS THE ESCALATION WORTH MARKING: it is the level at which energy stops being a background assumption in restart economics and becomes the deciding variable. THE SECOND-ORDER EFFECT IS DELIBERATELY NOT SUPPRESSED - the same escalation raises the energy and freight cost of producing and moving metal everywhere else, so it is bullish for price and bearish for margin simultaneously.

RE-ASSESSED 10-SEPTEMBER. HELD AT UP AND THE FRAGILITY INCREASED AGAIN WITHOUT ANY ALUMINA NUMBER MOVING. THE RISK AS WRITTEN IS AN ALUMINA COST SHOCK PROPAGATING INTO SMELTER MARGIN. Alunorte, the world's largest alumina refinery outside China, is back at full capacity from its August cut to 50% ON A TEMPORARY TERMINAL-ACCESS AGREEMENT WITH ITS GAS SUPPLIER. THE WORD TEMPORARY IS THE WHOLE EXPOSURE AND THE ENVIRONMENT AROUND IT DETERIORATED FOR A THIRD CONSECUTIVE SESSION: it is a gas arrangement, and European gas rose 3.97% with Brent through $100. A TEMPORARY GAS ACCOMMODATION IS MORE FRAGILE IN A TIGHTENING GAS MARKET THAN IN A LOOSENING ONE. NO NEWER DATED PUBLIC ALUMINA ASSESSMENT PRINTED THIS RUN and the FOB East Australia row is carried at its 05-August trade of $356/t with the date shown so the staleness is visible; an apparently newer index correction quoting $338.15/t was rejected because its stated date of 11-September is in the future and it is therefore a prior-year notice. SMM SEPARATELY EXPECTS THE SEPTEMBER MONTHLY AVERAGE ALUMINA PRICE TO DECLINE on surplus and continued inventory buildup, WHILE PREBAKED ANODE AND ALUMINIUM FLUORIDE BOTH RISE, and the energy tape now pushes the same way as the auxiliaries rather than against them. THE COST STACK IS MOVING IN AT LEAST THREE DIRECTIONS AT ONCE and total cash cost is not readable from the alumina headline alone. Bauxite remains the least-watched and most geographically concentrated link, at roughly two tonnes of alumina per tonne of metal.

RE-ASSESSED 10-SEPTEMBER. HELD AT FLAT. THE RISK AS WRITTEN IS THAT CHINESE EXPORT SUPPLY RELIEVES THE WESTERN SHORTAGE FASTER THAN THE BALANCE FORECASTS ASSUME, AND IT REMAINS THE MOST UNDER-WEIGHTED BEARISH FACT ON THIS PAGE. Exports rose 18.7% year on year in July, with public commentary attributing the surge to muted domestic demand allowing producers to ship out despite Beijing's 45-million-tonne output cap. THE MECHANISM MATTERS MORE THAN THE NUMBER: the relieving metal arrives as semi-finished and alloy product that does not pass through LME warehouses, which is one coherent explanation for how a thirty-six-year exchange inventory low can coexist with a warehouse series that has not moved a tonne across four published readings. TWO THINGS CONTINUE TO ARGUE AGAINST RAISING IT. FIRST, THERE IS STILL NO NEWER DATA - the July export figure is the latest public print and has now been carried unchanged for several runs, so any increase would be drift rather than evidence, and the staleness is stated rather than glossed. SECOND, THE CURVE ARGUES AGAINST THE STRONG FORM OF THE THESIS MORE FORCEFULLY THIS RUN THAN LAST: if ample Chinese semi-finished metal were satisfying Western prompt demand, the front of the aluminium curve should not have widened its backwardation on three consecutive sessions to a five-week high. The export flow explains the flat inventory; it does not explain the tightening curve.

RE-ASSESSED 10-SEPTEMBER. HELD AT UP, AND THE UNDERLYING FACT GOT WORSE WHILE ITS CONSEQUENCE GOT MORE AMBIGUOUS STILL. THE RISK AS WRITTEN IS THAT THE INVENTORY ARGUMENT UNDERPINNING THE BULL CASE STOPS WORKING. Exchange stock was UNCHANGED at 244,525 tonnes on 09-September - a published change of exactly ZERO for the THIRD consecutive session and the FOURTH consecutive published reading at the identical number - and has fallen just 2,400 tonnes across the fifteen sessions from 19-August to 09-September, about 160 tonnes per session, ALL OF IT BEFORE 04-SEPTEMBER. LEVEL AND FLOW HAVE NOW FULLY SEPARATED: the thirty-six-year low is real and remains the strongest single support for the price, but the draw that produced it has stopped completely. A market being drained does not print the same tonne four times running. THE REASON THIS IS HELD AT UP RATHER THAN RAISED IS THE COUNTER-EVIDENCE, WHICH HAS NOW ACCUMULATED ACROSS THREE SESSIONS RATHER THAN ONE: the curve tightened on every one of them, widening its backwardation from a $0.50 contango to $14.00 on stock that never moved, which suggests the bull case does not depend on the inventory flow as exclusively as this risk assumes. THE PRACTICAL READ IS UNCHANGED: until the London flow resumes, the inventory statistic should be treated as a floor under the price rather than as a trigger for the next leg higher. THE COUNTER-EVIDENCE IS REPORTED FOR BALANCE: Shanghai inventories fell 3% week on week, so the two visible series still disagree.

RE-ASSESSED 10-SEPTEMBER. HELD AT DOWN, AND THE CASE FOR HOLDING IT THERE STRENGTHENED MATERIALLY - BUT ONE OF THE TWO SUPPORTING ARGUMENTS HAS BEEN WITHDRAWN. THE RISK AS WRITTEN IS THAT THE CURVE SIGNAL IS TOO SMALL TO ACT ON IN EITHER DIRECTION. Cash settled $14.00 ABOVE three-month on 09-September, a BACKWARDATION that MORE THAN DOUBLED from $6.00 and is the WIDEST SINCE 04-AUGUST. IT HAS NOW WIDENED ON THREE CONSECUTIVE SESSIONS - from a $0.50 contango on 04-September through $2.00 and $6.00 to $14.00 - AND ON EVERY ONE OF THEM EXCHANGE STOCK DID NOT MOVE BY A SINGLE TONNE. Three sessions is a short trend rather than a single observation, and that is the substantive reason the risk stays lowered. THE ARGUMENT BEING WITHDRAWN IS THE CROSS-METAL ONE, AND IT IS WITHDRAWN EXPLICITLY RATHER THAN QUIETLY: yesterday this page argued that aluminium was the ONLY metal on the board whose curve tightened and treated that as a distinguishing signal. TODAY FOUR OF THE FIVE TIGHTENED - zinc to $150.00, copper to $40.00 on a falling flat price, lead's contango narrowing to $37.00 - so the aluminium move is corroborated by the complex rather than distinguished from it, which is a weaker and more macro explanation. THE SCALE RESTRAINT REMAINS DELIBERATE AND UNCHANGED: $14.00 on a $3,352 metal is forty-two hundredths of one percent, against zinc's 3.58%, and the August average spread was a $1.60 contango. This is now actionable information with a three-session trend behind it; it is still not a regime.

RE-ASSESSED 10-SEPTEMBER. HELD AT UP. THE EU IMPORT BAN ON RUSSIAN PRIMARY ALUMINIUM TAKES EFFECT 31-DECEMBER-2026 AND IS THE LARGEST SCHEDULED STRUCTURAL EVENT ON THIS PAGE - now under sixteen weeks away. THE RISK AS WRITTEN IS A DISORDERLY EUROPEAN SUPPLY RESET. The European duty-unpaid premium is the price that must absorb it and it is NOT BEHAVING AS IF THE EVENT IS COMING: duty-unpaid was last assessed at $485/t, below its own trailing average of $519.10, and the published rationale for the lower Q4 Japanese producer offers explicitly cites SOFTER premiums in Europe. TWO READINGS ARE LIVE AND THE ASSESSMENT CADENCE IS TOO SLOW TO DISTINGUISH THEM: either the market has already sourced replacement units and the ban is priced, or the event is not yet in the price at all. The second reading is the risk, and it becomes harder to hedge the closer the date comes. THE SECOND-ORDER PRESSURE INCREASED AGAIN THIS RUN AND ON THE SAME MORNING AS A POLICY DECISION: European gas firmed 3.97% for a third consecutive session, roughly 8.3% cumulatively, and the European Central Bank tightens TODAY - so the region that must absorb a supply shock at year end faces rising energy cost and a rising policy rate simultaneously, which narrows the room for European restarts to supply the replacement units. Slovalco's Q4-2026 restart, which begins in three weeks, is the nearest European supply addition and sits directly in that squeeze.

RE-ASSESSED 10-SEPTEMBER. HELD AT DOWN AND THE SOURCE STATE WAS CLEAN FOR A SECOND CONSECUTIVE MORNING, WHICH HAS NOT HAPPENED SINCE JULY. THE RISK AS WRITTEN IS SOURCE-DATA INTEGRITY: that the public price source this page depends on fails to publish, publishes stale cached snapshots, or disagrees with itself. THIS MORNING IT DID NONE OF THOSE THINGS. The English and cache-busted German overview pages both carry the 09-September board and agree line for line across all six metals, all six warehouse lines and all three EUR/USD fixings, AND ALL FIVE PER-METAL DAILY TABLES CARRY 09-SEPTEMBER AND REPRODUCE THE OVERVIEW EXACTLY. NO ROW REQUIRED ARITHMETIC RECONCILIATION. The stock identity balances five out of five to the tonne against the prior session plus published changes. AN INDEPENDENT REFERENCE DIVERGED MORE THAN USUAL AND IT IS DISCLOSED RATHER THAN SMOOTHED: Trading Economics carried aluminium at $3,327.98 for the 09-September session, DOWN 0.28%, which is $10.02 from the LME three-month official and in the OPPOSITE direction to it. The two are not the same instrument - one is a continuous intraday contract-for-difference mark, the other a ring settlement - so a divergence of this size on a session that moved is expected, but the page states it rather than choosing the flattering comparison. A SEPARATE INTEGRITY CATCH IS RECORDED THIS RUN: an alumina index correction quoting $338.15/t FOB Australia carried a stated date of 11-September, which is tomorrow, so it was identified as a prior-year notice and excluded. IT IS HELD AT DOWN RATHER THAN CLOSED because the page still depends on a single primary price source, and the caching and publication-lag failures of 31-July, 04-August and late August were characteristics of that source rather than one-off events.

balance.label: Deficit - Goldman -720 kt, Norsk Hydro -900 kt, Macquarie -930 kt; Citi an outlier at -2.7 Mt. THE BALANCE VIEW IS UNCHANGED BUT THE 19-AUGUST DATA SHARPENS HOW A DEFICIT CAN COEXIST WITH A LOOSENING FRONT END. Refined production outside China has fallen year on year for a second consecutive quarter and output outside China fell 6.7% year on year in July, so the annual deficit is real. Yet LME warrant has now been exactly unchanged on two consecutive sessions and the cash-3M spread has printed a widening contango on both. A deficit is an annual flow concept; a contango is a statement about prompt availability at a specific delivery point. THE RECONCILIATION MOST CONSISTENT WITH THE EVIDENCE, AND IT IS A HYPOTHESIS RATHER THAN A FACT, is that visible ex-China exchange stock is reported to be overwhelmingly Russian-origin material Western buyers cannot use - in which case the exchange series measures something different from accessible Western metal, and a global deficit can coexist with an LME front end that will not pay for prompt delivery. Supporting that reading, the Chinese physical market tightened on 20-August even as the LME curve loosened, with holders withholding and spot quotations firming to a small premium, and SHFE warrants continue to draw at roughly double the LME's monthly rate.

The published restart schedule is the reason, and it gained another dated entry on 20-August. Nanshan Aluminum's 2026 semi-annual report confirms 250,000 t/y of Indonesian aluminium and 260,000 t/y of carbon under construction at Bintan Industrial Park, with the integrated anode carbon removing one of the genuine physical constraints on commissioning new non-Chinese capacity. Alongside it: Gulf pre-incident output guided for Q1-2027 and running faster than the market expected; Slovalco 75,000 t/y from Q4-2026; Magnitude 7 Metals 75,000 t/y before year-end; Mount Holly already at full capacity and lifting US primary output by close to 10%; the Australian smelter's power secured to 2038 removing a closure risk over up to 590,000 t/y; Alunorte back at full rate; and a 500,000 t/y integrated Saudi greenfield through all compliance approvals with construction under way. These are published commitments with dates attached rather than projections, which is why the deficit is expected to narrow rather than persist at 2026 scale.

AN INDEPENDENT REFERENCE DIVERGED MORE THAN USUAL THIS RUN AND IT IS DISCLOSED RATHER THAN SMOOTHED: Trading Economics carried aluminium at $3,327.98 for the 09-September session, DOWN 0.28%, which is $10.02 from the LME three-month official and in the OPPOSITE direction. AN APPARENTLY NEWER ALUMINA MARK WAS FOUND AND DELIBERATELY REJECTED. A search returned an alumina index correction quoting $338.15/t FOB Australia with a stated date of 11-September, which is TOMORROW and therefore cannot be a 2026 assessment; it is a prior-year notice and it has NOT been used. The alumina row is carried at its last dated public trade of $356/t on 05-August with the date shown.

SPREAD CONVENTION, STATED EXPLICITLY BECAUSE THE SIGN CHANGES THE MEANING: cash ABOVE three-month is BACKWARDATION and indicates prompt tightness; cash BELOW three-month is CONTANGO. Aluminium settled a $14.00 BACKWARDATION on 09-September. Where spread and flat price move in OPPOSITE directions this page flags it explicitly - on this board that applies to COPPER, whose flat price fell while its backwardation widened.

PREMIUM ASSESSMENTS ARE PERIODIC RATHER THAN DAILY AND ARE CARRIED AT THEIR LAST PUBLIC MARK WITH THE ASSESSMENT DATE ATTACHED. They are NOT rolled forward, interpolated or adjusted to track the exchange price. The tariff decomposition IS recomputed every run against the current exchange cash, which means the implied market leg can move on a day when no premium was reassessed - that is an arithmetic artefact and is labelled as one.

THE PENDING OCTOBER-DECEMBER ASIAN QUARTERLY PREMIUM RANGE OF $290-325 IS HELD, NOT NARROWED, FOR AN EIGHTH CONSECUTIVE RUN. Both bounds are quoted numbers from the same dated 02-September-2026 report - the top of the published producer offer and the published buyer target. No dated public report newer than that was retrievable this morning, and this page does not tighten a published range on judgement alone.

A STALE ARTICLE CIRCULATING ON THE JAPANESE PREMIUM IS DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED: a widely-linked piece headlined 'Buyers push back; premiums slip' carries a dateline of 17-October-2025 and describes a different negotiation at $80-103/t. It is a prior-year article and it has not been used.

INPUT-BASKET TREND SERIES ARE BUILT FROM PUBLICLY SOURCED MARKS ON ONE CONSISTENT BASIS PER ROW, STATED ON THE ROW. GAPS ARE LEFT AS GAPS - nothing is interpolated or estimated - so a sparse two-or-three-point series on a periodic settlement row is the correct representation of the data rather than a defect. A regional East China spot anode quotation of RMB 5,230/t was seen this morning and was NOT appended, because this row is built on the national settlement basis and mixing bases would corrupt the trend.

THREE INPUT ROWS CARRY NO TREND SERIES AT ALL - smelter power, cathode and graphite blocks, and Ti-B grain refiner - because no public, dated, consistently-based series exists for them. AN EMPTY SPARKLINE MEANS NO PUBLIC DATA, NOT NO MOVEMENT.
